title: A Kid Reinstalled the TV App — Now the Store Is Locked | vitalii.no
description:
How reinstalling a TV kiosk app from the Play Store exposed a gap that guard scripts never covered, and how it got closed.

Someone at the TV stick reinstalled the kiosk app straight from the Play Store, which reset its settings and walked through Android's own permission dialogs to re-enable itself. The guard script blocked YouTube and Spotify just fine, but nothing stopped a kid from opening the Play Store or the Settings app directly and undoing the whole parental setup from the inside — a gap the lock screen was never built to see.

The fix adds a parent-only list of system apps — the Play Store, Android Settings, and the permission and installer dialogs — to the home-PC guard script, written in Python, checked on every cycle of the loop that already polls the foreground app. The moment one of those apps comes to the front without a parent's free-viewing mode or an active QR pass, the same lock screen fires that already covers a blocked YouTube or Spotify. Nothing else on the stick or phone changes, so a Wi-Fi setup screen during a reboot is never mistaken for a kid trying to sneak around.

The result: the Play Store, Settings, and every install dialog now kick back to the lock screen exactly like a locked app would — the one gap left in the system is now zero.
